key_insight: A graph neural network trained on smaller GW calculations predicts accurate quasiparticle energy levels in large transition metal dichalcogenide supercells at a fraction of the computational cost.
engineering_relevance: The approach could make accurate electronic-structure calculations more practical for large defect, surface, and moiré models where direct GW calculations become prohibitive.
method: Represent atoms as graph nodes and interatomic distances as edges.
Use DFT wavefunction projections onto localized atomic orbitals as input features.
Build a targeted, compact GW training dataset and tune hyperparameters with Bayesian optimization.
evidence_signal: For monolayer MoS₂ with a sulfur vacancy, the abstract reports mean absolute errors of 10–50 meV in predicted quasiparticle energy levels.
watch_item: Accuracy beyond the demonstrated MoS₂ vacancy system remains to be established, and training data must capture the physics of each target application.
paper_title: Graph Neural Networks for Accurate Quasiparticle Energy Levels in Large Supercells of Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
